title: Del moto e misura dell'acqua
shelf_note: Leonardo da Vinci's hydraulics treatise, 1828 Bologna edition: early modern science, which fits the library. But its only collection is 'americana', which it has nothing to do with (probably an Internet Archive collection tag carried over).
structure_note: The 'pages_translated' field (232) disagrees with the counted translated pages (304). The 19 printed-page backsteps are probably printed numerals misread on plate leaves (these pages cite fig./tav. plates) rather than a splice; the run 346-347-348 reads in order.

ocr_errors.image: dove tale onda è crea[ta] (right edge clipped)
ocr_errors.problem: the clipped word is completed wrongly as 'cres', and the translation then reads it as 'has grown' instead of 'is created'

tr_errors.source: la maggiore è sospinta dalla minore, quando essa si trova di minor potenza
tr_errors.english: the larger is pushed by the smaller when the latter possesses less power
tr_errors.problem: 'essa' refers to the larger body of water, which yields when IT has less power; 'the latter' points to the smaller and makes the sentence contradict itself

tr_errors.source: verso l'accrescimento della corrente
tr_errors.english: toward the acceleration of the current
tr_errors.problem: 'accrescimento' means growth or swelling, not acceleration

other.note: An editorial note invents context: it says Leonardo refers to a proposition 'he established earlier in his notebook regarding the angle at which water enters a whirlpool'. That is a plausible gloss, but the page does not say it.

ocr_errors.image: nello scontro c[on] (clipped at right edge)
ocr_errors.problem: The right edge of the scan is clipped on many lines. The OCR transcribes the truncated words faithfully ('del / nale', 'retros', 'oppre') and flags this in a <warning>, which is honest but leaves a broken text.

tr_errors.source: l'acqua che ruina [da] tale bassezza
tr_errors.english: The water that falls from such a depth
tr_errors.problem: the translation silently supplies the clipped words. That is reasonable, but the reader is not told which words were supplied.

other.note: The OCR's <warning> about truncated text ('Text on the right edge of the page appears to be truncated...') is copied into the translation pane, and an <unclear>of</unclear> tag appears inline in the English

book_verdict: The transcription and translation are good, and an expert would accept this text. The defects are a clipped right margin on the scan of p.348, a pipeline warning that leaks into the reader, and a collection tag ('americana') that does not fit the book.

title: 御定佩文韻府·卷九十三之五 (vol 664)
shelf_note: A Siku Quanshu reprint of the Peiwen Yunfu, a Qing rhyme thesaurus (卷九十三之五, the 秩 entries). It sits in the general 'universallibrary' collection: a reference work, outside the core traditions but not wrong for the library.
structure_note: Only 22 of 129 pages carry a printed number. The 8 backsteps and 10 repeats are most likely leaf numerals misread from the fold (on p.39 the OCR gives '六' for the printed 十八, and on p.40 it gives '一' as page number), not a splice. The block numerals in this run (十八, [十九 missing on p.40], 十九) are consistent.

ocr_errors.problem: headword misread, which turns 'promotion in rank' into 'high rank'

ocr_errors.image: 以昭忠義之勸 ... 有差 ... 吾用汝嘉併超丨丨 ... 馬有丨丨
ocr_errors.problem: The 丨丨 marks stand for the headword inside each quotation; dropping them leaves every citation without its key word. The columns are also scrambled: '顏延 / 寔計功量罪 / 之赭白馬賦' interleaves text from two neighbouring columns.

tr_errors.problem: 粟秩 is 'grain rations', not 'Full Rank'. The source says the horses have grain rations; the clause 'the ruler cannot maintain his position' is invented to complete the sentence.

tr_errors.problem: The Lunheng quotation belongs under 卑秩 ('lowly rank'). It is placed under 'Many Ranks', and its point (Zhou and Guan received a LOWLY rank) is lost. From here on the headwords and their citations are shifted one place: Xie Lingyun's 辭滿豈多秩 is filed under 'Gracious Rank'.

tr_errors.english: ### Pure and Clean / ### Poor Rank / Xue Tinggui's ... The Five Weapons are in **Pure and Clean** order
tr_errors.problem: A continuation line from the previous page is made into two invented headwords. The real headword 重秩 is dropped, and 'Pure and Clean' is substituted for it inside Xue Tinggui's decree.

book_verdict: A Chinese reader would flag this on sight. On two of the three pages PaddleOCR dropped the 丨丨 marks that stand for the headword, so the translation fills the gaps by inventing words, files citations under the wrong headwords, and creates headwords that do not exist ('Outer Rank', 'Pure and Clean'). Raw tags also show in the reader.

title: Carmen gratulatorium in natalem domini et salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi, compositum a Paulo donrspergero styro.
shelf_note: A Neo-Latin Christmas poem by Paul Dornsperger, 1573 (from MDZ). It has no collection or tradition assigned; it is in-period Latin verse but outside the core esoteric shelves. The title field's 'donrspergero' mirrors the source title (display title corrected).
structure_note: Of 20 pages, 15 are translated, so 5 pages lack English. Nothing else stands out; the catchwords (Contigerat → Contigerat, Huc → Huc) confirm that the run is in order.

tr_errors.source: Iam nouies centum ter mille recursibus annos / Aureus explerat Phoebus, terque inde vicenos / Addiderat
tr_errors.english: golden Phoebus had completed years by nine hundred times three thousand recursions, and had added twenty from there
tr_errors.problem: The source gives 3,900 years plus three times twenty (60), a date of 3960 years from Creation for the Nativity. The English multiplies 900 by 3000 and drops 'ter', so the date is wrong.

tr_errors.source: Deieci (Diuum sibi quod poscebat honorem / Maioremque illo) vobis fuit author edendi
tr_errors.english: I cast down (because he demanded for himself the honor of the Gods, and greater than that of the Gods) was the author for you to pluck
tr_errors.problem: The relative clause is lost: '[he whom] I cast down ... was the one who persuaded you to eat'. Because the line continues from the previous page, the English reads ungrammatically.

tr_errors.source: erecto spectantes lumine caelum
tr_errors.english: looking at heaven with raised light
tr_errors.problem: 'lumen' here means eyes ('with upturned gaze'); the literal rendering is opaque

other.note: The <sig>B 3</sig> tag and the catchword are carried in the OCR; the translation is clean

ocr_errors.problem: the catchword is tagged as a signature

tr_errors.source: Signa etiam doceo vos condita mente tenete
tr_errors.english: I also teach you to hold the signs in a conceived mind
tr_errors.problem: this should read 'I tell you the signs too: keep them stored in your mind'; the English is clumsy and literal

tr_errors.source: Quamuis innumeri
tr_errors.english: although countless [in power]
tr_errors.problem: the bracketed gloss is invented

book_verdict: The OCR is excellent and the translation is generally faithful, but it gets the poem's chronology wrong: it reads 3,900 + 60 years from Creation as 'nine hundred times three thousand ... added twenty'. Anyone who reads the Latin would catch it.

title: Sepher Yetzirah (Book of Formation) - Westcott
shelf_note: W. W. Westcott's English translation of the Sepher Yetzirah (2nd ed., 1893, University of Michigan copy). It is Golden Dawn-era Kabbalah, squarely in scope; the collections are 'opensource' and 'community'.
structure_note: The record count disagrees with the stored fields: there are 97 page records, all with OCR and translation, but pages_count, pages_ocr and pages_translated all say 43. Either the book was re-imported without the counters updating, or two scans were merged. The single printed backstep is probably the start of the main text after the front matter. Page 4's image comes from enhanced/ while its neighbours come from archived/, which is harmless.

tr_errors.source: and render this abstruse treatise more comprehensible than it has been hitherto found
tr_errors.english: making this complex <note>original: "abstruse"</note> treatise more understandable than it has been found until now
tr_errors.problem: An English source is 'translated' into paraphrased English. Westcott's own words are replaced ('forsaken' → 'abandoned', 'extended' → 'expanded'), so a reader quoting the English pane misquotes him.

other.note: The 'Digitized by UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN' watermark is carried into both panes as <meta>

tr_errors.source: # SEPHER YETZIRAH.
tr_errors.english: # THE BOOK OF FORMATION.
tr_errors.problem: the printed heading is changed

tr_errors.source: an aspect at once archaic and essentially Hebrew ... instructive philosophical treatise
tr_errors.english: a perspective that is both ancient and characteristically Hebrew ... educational philosophical treatise
tr_errors.problem: the whole page is rewritten rather than reproduced

tr_errors.source: Splendour ... treaties
tr_errors.english: Splendor ... treatises
tr_errors.problem: a same-language edit: the spelling is Americanised and Westcott's 'treaties' is silently corrected

other.note: The English text carries heavy glosses on every term (<note> for Sephiroth, Macroprosopus, Microcosm). That is harmless, but it is clutter added to an English original.

book_verdict: The OCR of this English book is clean. But an English source has been run through 'translation', which rewrites Westcott's own words and even changes a heading. The page counters disagree with the record count (43 vs 97).

title: The Pillow-Book of Sei Shōnagon
shelf_note: Arthur Waley's 1928 English translation of a Heian court diary, in the 'internetarchivebooks' collection only. It is a modern translation of a Japanese literary classic, outside the library's historical-sources focus, and it is not the original text.
structure_note: Of 172 pages, 171 are 'translated', but the translation is an English echo of English. The page sequence is clean (0 backsteps).

other.note: The 'translation' is a verbatim echo of the English OCR, and raw <header> and <sig>E</sig> tags show in the translation text

tr_errors.english: Shikibu no Omoto <note>one of the Empress's ladies</note>
tr_errors.problem: Waley's in-text bracket is turned into a pop-up note

other.note: A raw <header> tag shows in the translation pane, which echoes the English

ocr_errors.image: footnote ¹ at foot of page
ocr_errors.problem: a footnote is tagged as a margin note

tr_errors.source: Noritaka,¹ ... ¹ Brother-in-law of Murasaki
tr_errors.english: Noritaka, <note>Brother-in-law of Murasaki...</note> ... <margin>¹ Brother-in-law of Murasaki...</margin>
